key: Feedback Control + Free Energy Principle + Immune Systems

concepts.name: Feedback Control
concepts.short_description: Using output error to adjust input; PID controllers, stability margins, Bode plots, Nyquist criterion.

concepts.name: Free Energy Principle
concepts.short_description: Biological systems minimize variational free energy; prediction error minimization, Markov blankets.

concepts.name: Immune Systems
concepts.short_description: Adaptive defense via clonal selection and memory; antibody diversity, self/non-self discrimination.

hypotheses.statement: The self is a learned setpoint: negative selection builds the prior of a generative model by deleting whatever matches experienced inputs, and control action fires on residual matches. Tests whether a setpoint learned by deletion behaves differently from one learned by density estimation.

A conserved sensitivity budget: the Bode waterbed says attenuation in one band costs amplification elsewhere; a finite repertoire and the FEP complexity cost suggest that tolerance in one region of input space must create blindness or over-reaction in another. Tests whether sensitivity is redistributed, not created, by learning.

Precision is a population: the gain on a prediction error is the size of the clone that detects it, so learning precision is clonal expansion and runaway precision is a cytokine storm, i.e. a loop-stability failure predictable from Nyquist. Tests stability margins of population-coded gain under delay.

The Markov blanket is not a given structure but a controlled variable maintained by a patrolling detector population; the system's identity persists only while the patrol keeps boundary leakage below a threshold. Tests boundary persistence as a function of patrol density.

Inference by clonal competition: the recognition density is a population of hypotheses whose frequencies are updated by replication proportional to prediction accuracy and whose parameters are refined by error-scaled hypermutation. Tests whether a replicator population tracks the Bayes posterior and how it re-tracks after change.

Immune memory is an integral term: original antigenic sin is integrator windup, and anergy is an anti-windup rule. Tests whether memory strength vs drift reproduces a windup signature and whether an anti-windup clamp restores performance.

Three different triggers compete: control acts on error to a setpoint, FEP acts on surprise, immunity acts on damage/danger. Tests which trigger signal yields least harm per unit of response under novel-but-harmless vs familiar-but-harmful inputs.

Tolerance-by-deletion setpoint: during a developmental window a random detector repertoire is exposed to the system's own inputs and every detector that fires is deleted; after the window, any detector firing drives corrective action. The setpoint is the complement of the surviving repertoire.

concept_contributions.Feedback Control: error-driven corrective action after the window
concept_contributions.Free Energy Principle: the surviving repertoire is an implicit prior; firing = high surprisal
concept_contributions.Immune Systems: negative selection of a random repertoire

knockouts.Feedback Control: no action is taken; the mechanism becomes a pure anomaly detector
knockouts.Free Energy Principle: loses the link between detection rate and surprisal; weak effect on the testable world
knockouts.Immune Systems: no deletion: the setpoint is not learned and detectors fire on self (autoimmunity)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Novelty detection by distance threshold to stored training samples (kNN density).

hypotheses.statement: Waterbed repertoire allocation: total detector mass is fixed; expanding coverage (sensitivity) in one region of input space must reduce it elsewhere, so the summed log-sensitivity over input space is approximately conserved under learning.

concept_contributions.Feedback Control: the Bode integral as the conservation law
concept_contributions.Free Energy Principle: complexity cost as the price of sensitivity
concept_contributions.Immune Systems: finite niche and competition for survival signals

knockouts.Feedback Control: no conservation law to test; becomes an ordinary capacity limit
knockouts.Free Energy Principle: loses the reading of sensitivity as precision; still testable
knockouts.Immune Systems: no finite repertoire; nothing forces redistribution

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Any fixed-capacity classifier trades recall between classes.

questions.what_exists: detector mass distributed over input bins
questions.distinguishing_observable: summed log-sensitivity across bins stays within a band while individual bins shift by large factors

hypotheses.statement: Clonal gain loop: controller gain equals the size of the responding clone; the clone grows in proportion to delayed error and decays at a cost rate. The loop has a delay-dependent oscillatory instability (storm) whose onset is predicted by the Nyquist criterion of the linearised loop.

concept_contributions.Feedback Control: Nyquist/delay stability analysis of the loop
concept_contributions.Free Energy Principle: gain read as precision on the prediction error

knockouts.Feedback Control: no predictive stability theory; only simulation
knockouts.Free Energy Principle: weak: the mechanism is fully specified without FEP, which only renames gain as precision
knockouts.Immune Systems: gain is a fixed parameter; no storm

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: MIT-rule adaptive gain controller with delay; Lotka-Volterra with delay.

questions.what_persists: the equilibrium if stable, a limit cycle if not
questions.distinguishing_observable: critical delay tau* measured vs predicted from the linearisation

hypotheses.statement: Precision-as-clone-count: each prediction-error channel is weighted by the number of detectors assigned to it, so precision is integer-valued and learned by birth-death rather than by gradient.

knockouts.Feedback Control: weights are only for inference, not action
knockouts.Free Energy Principle: no reason to call counts precision; weights become arbitrary
knockouts.Immune Systems: precision is a continuous parameter with gradient updates

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Learned per-channel weights by any running inverse-variance estimator.

questions.what_can_transfer: counts as priors for a new task
questions.distinguishing_observable: count ratios converge to inverse noise-variance ratios; demographic noise makes low-count channels fluctuate in a way a continuous estimator does not

hypotheses.statement: Replicator inference: the recognition density is a finite population of hypothesis clones; each step clones replicate in proportion to exp(-prediction error) and mutate with a rate scaled by their current error.

concept_contributions.Free Energy Principle: population frequencies as q(s); free energy as objective

knockouts.Feedback Control: no closed loop on the world; pure inference
knockouts.Free Energy Principle: no normative target (exact posterior) to compare to
knockouts.Immune Systems: no population; becomes a single gradient-updated estimate

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: A bootstrap particle filter with jitter (sequential Monte Carlo). Likely the same mechanism.

questions.what_can_transfer: the population as a warm start
questions.distinguishing_observable: KL between clone frequencies and exact posterior; re-tracking time after a switch under error-scaled vs constant mutation

hypotheses.statement: Antigenic-sin windup: stored memory clones respond first and consume the antigen that naive clones need to be selected, so after drift the response stays locked to the old target. An anti-windup rule suppresses memory recall when error is not falling.

concept_contributions.Free Energy Principle: an overly precise prior that resists update
concept_contributions.Immune Systems: memory cells competing with naive cells

knockouts.Feedback Control: no anti-windup design; only the failure is described
knockouts.Free Energy Principle: weak: the precision reading adds vocabulary, not a new prediction
knockouts.Immune Systems: no memory; nothing to wind up

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Stale prior / momentum in any online learner.

questions.what_exists: memory and naive clones, drifting antigen
questions.what_can_learn: the new antigen, if memory releases
questions.distinguishing_observable: clearance time vs drift distance shows a threshold under memory that is absent under randomly placed memory

hypotheses.statement: Blanket-by-patrol: the boundary between inside and outside exists only while a population of mobile detectors removes intruding non-self elements; blanket integrity is itself the controlled variable.

concept_contributions.Feedback Control: regulation of leakage to a setpoint
concept_contributions.Free Energy Principle: the Markov blanket and its conditional independence as the measured quantity

knockouts.Feedback Control: no setpoint on leakage; patrol is open-loop
knockouts.Free Energy Principle: no measure of what the boundary achieves (conditional MI)
knockouts.Immune Systems: nothing removes intruders; the boundary dissolves

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: A wall with a repair rate.

questions.what_persists: the interior, if patrol is sufficient
questions.what_can_reproduce: patrols, if recruited in proportion to intrusions
questions.distinguishing_observable: a sharp transition in blanket persistence and in I(inside; outside | boundary) as patrol density crosses a threshold

hypotheses.statement: Danger-gated learning: model updates and actions are licensed by a damage signal (realised harm), not by surprise or error, so novel-but-harmless input is tolerated and familiar-but-harmful input is attacked.

concept_contributions.Feedback Control: error as the action variable once licensed
concept_contributions.Free Energy Principle: surprise as the ungated alternative trigger

knockouts.Immune Systems: no damage channel; collapses to surprise gating

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Reward-gated learning (reinforcement learning with a harm cost). Displaced as default ontology: here the gate is a binary licence, not a value to maximise.

questions.what_changes: model and action, only when licensed
questions.distinguishing_observable: harm per unit response under a mix of harmless-novel and harmful-familiar inputs

hypotheses.statement: Idiotypic internal model: detectors that recognise other detectors form a network whose own oscillatory modes can embody the generator of a periodic disturbance, satisfying the internal model principle without an explicit oscillator.

knockouts.Feedback Control: no requirement that a generator copy be present; the network is just dynamics
knockouts.Immune Systems: no self-recognising network; needs an explicit oscillator

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: An explicit resonant filter tuned to the disturbance frequency.

questions.distinguishing_observable: steady-state rejection of a periodic disturbance only when a network mode matches its frequency

hypotheses.statement: Error-scheduled hypermutation: mutation step size is a feedback-controlled variable set by residual error, like annealing whose temperature is closed-loop.

knockouts.Free Energy Principle: weak: nothing FEP-specific; three-way dependency is weak

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Adaptive step size (1/5th success rule) in evolution strategies.

questions.distinguishing_observable: re-tracking time after a switch vs constant rate at matched mean

hypotheses.statement: Complement coding of expectation: prediction error is computed not as observation minus prediction but as the firing of a stored set of not-expected detectors; the model represents the complement of the expected.

knockouts.Free Energy Principle: loses the equivalence claim to prediction error

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Threshold on distance to nearest stored example.

questions.distinguishing_observable: scaling of detector count with dimension for fixed AUC vs kNN memory scaling

hypotheses.statement: Cross-reactivity bandwidth trade: broadly cross-reactive detectors act like high-bandwidth, low-precision feedback, narrow ones like narrow-band high-precision feedback; broad clones plus positive feedback produce autoimmune instability.
hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Kernel width in any nearest-neighbour detector.

questions.what_is_selected: widths that reduce error without self-attack
questions.distinguishing_observable: autoimmune events vs mean width, showing a threshold

hypotheses.statement: Innate/adaptive cascade: a fast fixed-gain loop holds the system while a slow learned loop sets the fast loop's setpoint, a timescale hierarchy as in hierarchical FEP. Three-way dependency weak: this is cascade control.

questions.distinguishing_observable: performance vs timescale ratio; expected to match cascade theory exactly

hypotheses.statement: Tolerance-inflammation hysteresis: positive feedback between damage and inflammation plus negative feedback from regulatory cells gives a bistable switch; the self/non-self boundary in input space shows hysteresis when the input is swept.

knockouts.Free Energy Principle: weak: FEP only relabels the two states

questions.distinguishing_observable: hysteresis loop area under forward vs backward sweep

hypotheses.statement: Sentinel repertoire: a fixed fraction of detectors is reserved for low-affinity epistemic sampling (expected information gain) and never expanded, to keep coverage of unseen regions.

knockouts.Free Energy Principle: no epistemic justification for the reserve

questions.distinguishing_observable: time to first detection of a novel threat vs reserve fraction

hypotheses.statement: Anergy as chronic precision down-regulation: when an error persists without falling, the responding clone's gain is reduced, preventing storm and windup at the cost of tolerating chronic error.

knockouts.Free Energy Principle: no reason to link to precision

questions.distinguishing_observable: increase of critical delay tau* and of chronic error level under exhaustion

lenses.name: Waterbed ledger
lenses.rationale: Invented for this triplicate: tests whether detector-mediated sensitivity obeys a conservation law analogous to the Bode integral.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: per-bin detector allocation and per-bin detection sensitivity over a discretised input space
lenses.transformation: compute S_b = missed-detection odds per bin; sum log S_b across bins before and after learning
predictedSignals: sum stays within +-10% while individual bins change by > 2x
lenses.nullExpectation: the sum moves freely with learning; no conservation beyond detector count
failureModes: conservation is just fixed detector count
bins too coarse to see redistribution
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: a conservation-law observable rather than a performance metric

lenses.name: Clone-Nyquist
lenses.rationale: Invented: linearise the population-gain loop and use classical stability theory as an a-priori prediction for a population process.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: delay-difference equations of pathogen and clone counts
lenses.transformation: linearise at equilibrium, form the open-loop transfer function, compute critical delay tau*
predictedSignals: observed onset within 15% of predicted tau*
lenses.nullExpectation: demographic noise or nonlinearity shifts onset unpredictably
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: a quantitative prediction made before simulation instead of a post-hoc fit

lenses.name: Tolerance hole map
lenses.rationale: Invented: maps regions of non-self that no surviving detector covers, as a function of dimension.
lenses.transformation: sample non-self; mark covered/uncovered by surviving detectors
predictedSignals: hole fraction rises sharply with L
lenses.nullExpectation: same curve for randomly drawn, undeleted detectors
failureModes: the matching rule, not deletion, dominates holes
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates deletion-induced blindness from generic sparsity

lenses.name: Blanket leakage audit
lenses.rationale: Measure the property that defines a Markov blanket directly rather than assuming it.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: time series of interior, boundary and exterior cell states
lenses.transformation: estimate conditional mutual information I(interior; exterior | boundary) with a plug-in estimator on binned states
predictedSignals: CMI low above a patrol-density threshold, high below
lenses.nullExpectation: CMI varies smoothly with patrol density
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: tests the FEP-defining statistic, not just survival

lenses.name: Repertoire-as-posterior
lenses.rationale: Compare clone frequencies to an exact Bayesian posterior where one is computable.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: clone frequency histogram over a parameter grid
lenses.transformation: KL(clone histogram || exact posterior) per step
observables: re-tracking time after a regime switch
lenses.nullExpectation: identical to a particle filter with the same jitter
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: a normative yardstick for the population

lenses.name: Windup hysteresis loop
lenses.rationale: Invented: sweep antigen drift forward and backward and read the response-latency hysteresis as the windup signature.
lenses.transformation: latency vs drift distance on forward and reverse sweeps; loop area
predictedSignals: nonzero loop area under memory, near zero without memory
lenses.nullExpectation: loop area equal for randomly placed memory
failureModes: resource exhaustion rather than competition causes latency

lenses.name: Trigger-signal counterfactual
lenses.rationale: Invented: swap only the triggering signal (error, surprise, damage) holding all else fixed; the one variable the three concepts disagree on.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: input stream labelled harmless/harmful and novel/familiar
lenses.transformation: run three otherwise-identical agents with different triggers
predictedSignals: damage trigger lowest harm per response on decorrelated streams
lenses.nullExpectation: trigger choice irrelevant when harmfulness correlates with novelty

experiments.hypothesis: The onset of sustained oscillation (storm) in a delayed clonal-gain loop is predicted by the linearised Nyquist critical delay, and exhaustion (M16) raises the critical delay beyond what an equal mean-gain reduction does.
experiments.mechanism: Discrete-time stochastic loop: pathogen p grows at rate r and is killed at rate k*p*C; clone C grows at rate a*p(t - tau) and decays at rate c; an exhaustion variable reduces a when p has not fallen for T steps.
experiments.intervention: sweep delay tau over 40 values; toggle exhaustion on/off
experiments.control: fixed-gain controller with gain equal to the time-averaged k*C of the adaptive run (with and without exhaustion)
experiments.positive_control: linear delayed proportional loop with an analytic critical delay; the pipeline must recover it within 5%
experiments.observable: oscillation indicator: coefficient of variation of p over the last 2000 steps > 0.2; tau_obs = smallest tau with the indicator true in >= 50% of seeds
experiments.success_criterion: |tau_obs - tau_pred| / tau_pred <= 0.15 over 20 seeds AND tau_obs(exhaustion) / tau_obs(no exhaustion) >= 1.3 AND that ratio exceeds the matched fixed-gain control's ratio by >= 0.1
experiments.failure_criterion: relative error > 0.15, OR exhaustion ratio < 1.1, OR exhaustion ratio within 0.1 of the matched fixed-gain ratio, OR the positive control misses by > 5%
experiments.alternative_explanation: exhaustion simply lowers mean gain; any lower fixed gain would raise tau* equally
experiments.null_twin: clone counts replaced by a phase-randomised surrogate of the adaptive run's C(t) (same mean, variance and spectrum) decoupled from p; destroys the feedback while matching gain statistics
experiments.why_this_implementation: a stochastic population process keeps clone counts integer and expansion delayed, which is the peculiar immune structure; no learned model is needed
experiments.size: 1 pathogen, 1 clone population; 40 delays x 2 exhaustion settings x 20 seeds x 5000 steps
stupid_explanations: exhaustion only reduces mean gain (checked by the matched fixed-gain control)
stochastic extinction at low counts ends oscillation early and looks like stability
the CV threshold 0.2 is tuned to the result

experiments.hypothesis: A negative-selection repertoire matches a kNN density detector at equal memory in low dimension, but its detection AUC falls faster with dimension because deletion creates holes.
experiments.mechanism: random r-contiguous detectors over {0,1}^L; delete any that match a self sample; score test strings by the number of matching surviving detectors
experiments.intervention: vary L in {8, 12, 16, 20, 24}; hold stored bits equal between methods
experiments.control: kNN distance-to-self scorer with the same number of stored bits
experiments.positive_control: anomalies at Hamming distance > L/2 from all self: both methods must reach AUC >= 0.95
experiments.observable: ROC AUC on held-out self vs structured non-self; hole fraction; sum of log miss-odds across 16 input bins (L1)
experiments.success_criterion: mean AUC(negsel) >= mean AUC(kNN) - 0.02 at L <= 12 AND mean AUC(kNN) - mean AUC(negsel) >= 0.10 at L = 24 over 10 seeds AND negsel minus null-twin AUC >= 0.05 at L = 8
experiments.failure_criterion: negsel within 0.10 of kNN at L = 24, OR worse by > 0.02 at L <= 12, OR not >= 0.05 above the null twin at L = 8, OR positive control fails
experiments.alternative_explanation: the r-contiguous matching rule, not deletion, causes the drop
experiments.null_twin: same detector count and matching radius drawn randomly WITHOUT deletion (destroys tolerance learning, matches detector statistics)
experiments.why_this_implementation: a binary shape space with contiguous matching preserves the repertoire-and-deletion structure; a neural autoencoder (displaced) would replace deletion with a learned density and erase the mechanism
experiments.size: self set 200 strings, 2000 candidate detectors, 1000 test strings, 5 dimensions, 10 seeds
stupid_explanations: the non-self generator sits closer to self at high L, so every method drops
AUC dominated by ties in integer match counts

experiments.hypothesis: A clonal replicator population with error-scaled hypermutation approximates the exact posterior at stationarity and re-tracks faster after a regime switch than mutation of matched statistics that is not coupled to error.
experiments.mechanism: 256 hypothesis clones over the drift parameter of a 1D linear-Gaussian system; replicate proportional to exp(-squared prediction error); mutation sd proportional to each clone's recent error
experiments.intervention: switch the true parameter at step 1000; compare error-scaled vs constant mutation
experiments.control: bootstrap particle filter with constant jitter of the same time-averaged size
experiments.positive_control: exact grid posterior computed alongside; replicator with zero mutation and exact weights must reach KL < 0.02
experiments.observable: KL(clone histogram || grid posterior) on a 64-bin grid; re-tracking time = steps until posterior mean is within 1 sd of the new truth
experiments.success_criterion: median stationary KL < 0.1 nats AND median re-tracking time (error-scaled) <= 0.7 x both the constant-jitter control and the null twin, over 30 seeds
experiments.failure_criterion: KL >= 0.1, OR re-tracking ratio > 0.9 against either the control or the null twin
experiments.alternative_explanation: it is a particle filter with adaptive jitter; any adaptive jitter gives the speed-up
experiments.null_twin: mutation sd drawn from the same empirical distribution as the error-scaled run but permuted across clones and time (destroys error coupling, matches mutation statistics)
experiments.why_this_implementation: a finite replicating population keeps counts and lineages explicit, unlike a variational gradient method
stupid_explanations: larger mutation after the switch just raises exploration
grid coarseness makes KL small anyway
it is sequential Monte Carlo renamed

experiments.hypothesis: Memory clones that compete with naive clones for antigen produce a windup threshold in clearance time vs antigen drift, and an anti-windup rule restores clearance near the no-memory level.
experiments.mechanism: 2D shape space; antigen drifts by distance d between exposures; memory clones at the old position bind first and consume antigen in proportion to affinity; naive clones need antigen to expand
experiments.intervention: sweep d over 20 values forward and backward; toggle anti-windup (suppress memory if load has not halved within T steps)
experiments.positive_control: at d = 0 memory must clear at least 2x faster than no-memory
experiments.observable: clearance time; hysteresis loop area between forward and reverse sweeps
experiments.success_criterion: for some d* the memory clearance time exceeds 1.5x no-memory, the loop area is > 3x the null-twin area, AND anti-windup stays within 1.2x of no-memory at every d, over 20 seeds
experiments.failure_criterion: no d with memory > 1.5x no-memory, OR loop area <= 3x null, OR anti-windup > 1.2x no-memory at any d, OR positive control fails
experiments.alternative_explanation: memory simply depletes a shared resource, independent of history
experiments.null_twin: memory clones placed at random positions with the same count and affinity distribution (destroys history-specificity)
experiments.why_this_implementation: competition for antigen is the peculiar immune structure; an online gradient learner would hide it inside momentum
experiments.size: 500 naive clones, 50 memory clones; 20 drift values x 2 directions x 2 anti-windup settings x 20 seeds x 300 steps
stupid_explanations: anti-windup just deletes memory, making it identical to the control
the 1.5x threshold chosen after seeing curves
